examples.en: My Korean level is still beginner.
We take a level test and decide the class.
I'm happy because my level went up in the game.
This book is divided by level.
To raise your level you have to practice every day.
Try choosing a class that fits your level.

explain: 한국어 학원에서는 '급'이나 '단계'라는 말도 같이 써요. 게임이나 반 나누기에서 '레벨'이 자주 나와요. 실력 차이를 말할 때 '레벨이 다르다'고 하면 차이가 크다는 느낌이에요. 일반적인 수준 이야기에서는 '수준'도 써요.
explain_en: Korean language schools also use 급 and 단계 alongside it. 레벨 comes up often in games and when sorting classes. Saying 레벨이 다르다 about skill implies a big gap. For general standards, 수준 is also used.

examples.en: What made you so angry?
Why on earth did you go all the way there alone?
What's so important about that?

examples.ko: 이 일을 뭣부터 시작해야 할지 모르겠어요.
examples.en: I don't know what to start with first on this job.

examples.ko: 오늘은 뭣 하나 제대로 되는 게 없어요.
examples.en: Today, not a single thing is going right.

examples.ko: 이 많은 걸 뭣에 쓰려고 샀어요?
examples.en: What did you buy this much for?

explain: '무엇'을 줄인 '뭐'보다 조금 거칠거나 강조하는 느낌이 있어요. 주로 '뭣 때문에', '뭣 하러', '뭣도 모르고'처럼 굳은 짝으로 써요. 평소 말은 '뭐'가 자연스러워요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 사정을 전혀 모른 채 행동할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone acts without knowing the situation at all.

explain_en: It feels a little rougher or more emphatic than '뭐', the short form of '무엇'. It mostly appears in set pairs such as '뭣 때문에', '뭣 하러', and '뭣도 모르고'. In ordinary speech, '뭐' is more natural.

dis.h: clipped form used in set phrases

p.n: Same meaning; the replacement is the plain spoken form.

examples.ko: 이 단어는 쓰는 것과 다르게 발음되는 경우가 많아요.
examples.en: This word is often pronounced differently from how it's written.
The word for flower plus a subject marker is pronounced 'kkochi', so the final consonant links to the next syllable.
The name of the ancient kingdom Silla is pronounced 'Silla', so the sound differs from the spelling.
The ㅎ at the end of the syllable in the word for 'good' is not pronounced.

examples.ko: 외국인 이름은 한국어로 다르게 발음될 수 있어요.
examples.en: Foreign names can be pronounced differently in Korean.

examples.ko: 이 이름은 나라마다 다르게 발음되고 있어요.
examples.en: This name is pronounced differently in each country.

explain: '발음하다'는 사람이 소리 내는 것이고, '발음되다'는 글자나 단어가 어떤 소리로 나는지 말할 때 써요. '[꼬치]로 발음되다'처럼 소리를 대괄호로 함께 적기도 해요.
explain_en: '발음하다' is a person making the sound, while '발음되다' says what sound a letter or word comes out as. Learners often write the sound in square brackets, as in '[꼬치]로 발음되다'.

examples.ko: 고향 친구가 감을 한 상자 보내왔어요.
examples.en: A friend sent me a box of persimmons from their hometown.
Grandmother sends us kimchi every year.
The company sent the news that I passed by email.
Someone sent me a strange text message yesterday.

examples.ko: 외국에 있는 언니가 사진을 보내오면 가족이 다 모여서 봐요.
examples.en: When my older sister abroad sends photos, the whole family gathers to look.

examples.ko: 학교에서 안내문을 보내오면 꼭 읽어 보세요.
examples.en: If the school sends a notice, be sure to read it.

explain: '보내다'는 내가 보내는 것이고, '보내오다'는 상대가 나에게 보내서 도착하는 것이에요. 편지, 소식, 선물, 문자에 많이 써요. 내가 상대에게 보낼 때는 '보내다'나 '보내 주다'를 써요.
explain_en: '보내다' is when I send something, while '보내오다' is when the other person sends it and it reaches me. It is common with letters, news, gifts and text messages. When I send to someone, I use '보내다' or '보내 주다'.

en: counseling center; consultancy; counseling service agency

examples.en: If you have a worry, try going to a counseling center.

examples.ko: 이 상담소는 무료로 이야기를 들어 줘요.
examples.en: This counseling center listens to you for free.
The counseling center is on the third floor of the building.
My friend told me about a counseling center.
I talked with a counselor for an hour at the counseling center.
Some counseling centers also require a reservation.

explain: 고민이나 문제를 전문가와 이야기하러 가는 곳이에요. '법률 상담소', '청소년 상담소'처럼 앞에 분야를 붙여 써요. 학교 안에서는 '상담실'이라고 하기도 해요.
explain_en: It is a place where you go to talk about worries or problems with a professional. The field comes first, as in '법률 상담소' (legal) or '청소년 상담소' (youth). Inside a school it may be called '상담실'.

examples.en: I shake hands with people I meet for the first time.
Yesterday I shook hands with the new boss.
I will shake hands with the guest first tomorrow.
The hand I shook was very warm.
The two smiled, shook hands, and parted.
I was really happy to shake hands with my teacher.

explain: 악수하는 상대 뒤에 '와/과'나 '하고'를 붙여서 '친구와 악수하다'처럼 써요. '악수를 하다'로 띄어 써도 같아요.
explain_en: The other person takes '와/과' or '하고', as in '친구와 악수하다'. You can also split it as '악수를 하다' with the same meaning.

examples.en: The hotel room is already booked.

examples.ko: 이 자리는 다른 손님 이름으로 예약됐어요.
examples.en: This seat has been reserved under another guest's name.
Once it's booked, I'll let you know by text.
I went to the hospital at the booked time.
The ticket wasn't booked, so I applied again.
After the restaurant was booked, I told my friends.

explain: 자리나 시간이 이미 잡혀 있을 때 써요. '예약돼 있어요'가 가장 흔해요. 내가 하는 행동은 '예약하다'예요. 식당과 병원은 '예약', 친구와 만나는 일은 '약속'을 써요.
explain_en: It is used when a seat or time slot is already secured, and 예약돼 있어요 is the most common form. What you do yourself is 예약하다. Use 예약 for restaurants and clinics, and 약속 for meeting a friend.

examples.en: My sister-in-law is two years younger than me.
My mother and my sister-in-law cooked together.
I got hand-me-down kids' clothes from my sister-in-law.
I get along very well with my sister-in-law.
I brought a cake on my sister-in-law's birthday.
I called my sister-in-law to ask how she was.

explain: 여자가 남자 형제의 아내를 가리킬 때 쓰는 말이에요. 오빠의 아내를 직접 부를 때는 '새언니'라고 부르기도 해요. 남자가 형제의 아내를 말할 때는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: A woman uses it for her brother's wife. When directly addressing her older brother's wife, she may call her '새언니'. A man doesn't use it for his brother's wife.

examples.en: My second cousin came to the wedding.
You have fewer chances to meet second cousins than first cousins.
My second cousin goes to the same university.
I think relatives up to second cousins are close relatives.

examples.ko: 아버지 쪽 육촌과는 거의 연락을 안 해요.
examples.en: I hardly keep in touch with my second cousins on my father's side.
I sent a wedding invitation to my second cousin.

explain: '육촌 형', '육촌 동생'처럼 뒤에 형·누나·동생을 붙여 불러요. 촌수는 숫자가 클수록 먼 친척이에요. 사촌보다 한 단계 더 먼 사이라서 자주 못 만나는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: You add words after it, as in '육촌 형' or '육촌 동생'. The bigger the 촌수 number, the more distant the relative. It is a step more distant than a first cousin, so people often don't meet them much.

examples.en: A red light usually means danger.
Do you know what this sign means?
This photo means family to me.

examples.ko: 대답을 안 한다고 해서 동의를 의미하지는 않아요.
examples.en: Not answering doesn't mean you agree.

examples.ko: 그 편지는 저에게 새로운 시작을 의미했어요.
examples.en: That letter meant a new beginning for me.

examples.ko: 초록색은 보통 안전을 의미해서 비상구에 써요.
examples.en: Green usually signals safety, so it's used for emergency exits.

explain: 표지판, 색깔, 행동처럼 눈에 보이는 것이 무엇을 나타내는지 말할 때 잘 어울려요. 모르는 단어를 물을 때는 '의미해요?'보다 '무슨 뜻이에요?'라고 묻는 게 훨씬 자연스러워요. 명사 '의미'는 '의미가 있다/없다'처럼 가치를 말할 때도 써요.
explain_en: It fits things like signs, colors, and actions that signal something. When asking about an unknown word, '무슨 뜻이에요?' is much more natural than '의미해요?'. The noun '의미' also expresses value, as in '의미가 있다/없다' (it's meaningful or not).

en: deposit amount; payment on an account

examples.en: Check your account to see whether the deposit amount is right.
The deposit will arrive in the account today.
I wrote the deposit amount wrong by mistake.
Please email me the deposit confirmation.
The interest changes depending on the deposit amount.
Points are added automatically in proportion to the deposit amount.

explain: '금액'은 돈의 양이고 '입금액'은 계좌에 넣은 돈이에요. 반대는 '출금액'이고, 들어온 돈과 나간 돈을 같이 볼 때 짝으로 써요. 말할 때는 '입금한 돈'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: '금액' is an amount of money, and '입금액' is the money put into an account. The opposite is '출금액', and the two are used as a pair when looking at money in and out. In speech people also say '입금한 돈'.

examples.en: Why is that person acting like that?
That kind of behavior isn't good.
If he acts like that, his friends will dislike him.
I'm worried because my sibling is like that.
Many people came out even in weather like that.
I've never seen such a big dog.

explain: '이러하다, 그러하다, 저러하다'는 이것, 그것, 저것의 모양이나 상태를 가리키는 말이에요. 저러하다는 멀리 있는 것을 가리키고, 실제 말에서는 '저렇다'나 줄인 형태 '저래요', '저런', '저렇게'를 더 많이 써요. 글에서는 '저러한'도 볼 수 있어요.
explain_en: 이러하다, 그러하다, and 저러하다 refer to how something looks or is. 저러하다 points to something far away, and in speech people use the forms '저렇다', '저래요', '저런', and '저렇게' much more. '저러한' appears mostly in writing.

dis.h: like that; thing far from both

p.n: 이런 refers to clothes close to the speaker; 저런 refers to clothes far from speaker and listener.

examples.ko: 선생님께 이 편지를 꼭 전달해 주세요.
examples.en: Please make sure to pass this letter on to the teacher.
I passed my words on to my friend just as they were.
I pass the meeting notes on to the team by email.
I'll pass this news on to my mother today.

examples.ko: 이 소포는 내일까지 고객에게 전달해야 해요.
examples.en: This package has to be delivered to the customer by tomorrow.
If you pass it on by text message, it's faster and easier.

explain: '전하다'는 소식·마음·인사를 건넬 때 쓰고('안부를 전하다'), '전달하다'는 물건이나 업무 내용을 사무적으로 넘길 때 써요. 그래서 안부는 '전달해 주세요'보다 '전해 주세요'가 자연스러워요. 받는 사람이 윗사람이면 '~께'를 붙여요.
explain_en: '전하다' is for passing on news, feelings or greetings ('안부를 전하다'), while 전달하다 is for handing over objects or work information in a businesslike way. So for greetings, '전해 주세요' sounds more natural than '전달해 주세요'. If the receiver is senior to you, use '~께' instead of '~에게'.

examples.en: The cat approaches carefully.
A stranger suddenly approached me.
Try approaching this problem differently.
I can hear a car approaching.
It is dangerous, so you must not get close.

examples.ko: 더 쉽게 접근할 수 있는 방법이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a way to approach it more easily.

explain: 장소로 다가갈 때도 쓰고, 문제를 어떻게 다룰지 말할 때도 써요. '문제에 접근하다'처럼 방법의 뜻이 있어요. '다가가다'는 더 부드럽고 일상적인 말이에요.
explain_en: It works for physically moving closer and also for how you handle a problem, as in 'approach an issue'. The plain verb for coming near sounds softer and more everyday.

examples.en: The nurse showed me to the examination room.
I waited in front of the examination room to be called.

examples.ko: 진찰실에 들어가면 의사 선생님께 증상을 말씀드리세요.
examples.en: When you go into the examination room, tell the doctor your symptoms.
The child cried in the examination room because she was scared.

examples.ko: 이 병원은 진찰실이 세 개 있어요.
examples.en: This clinic has three examination rooms.

examples.ko: 진찰실은 이 층 복도 끝에 있어요.
examples.en: The examination room is at the end of the hallway on the second floor.

explain: 병원에서 의사가 환자를 보는 방이고, 수술하는 '수술실'이나 약을 받는 '약국'과 달라요. 말할 때는 그냥 '안으로 들어가세요'라고도 많이 해요.
explain_en: It is the room where a doctor sees patients, different from '수술실' (operating room) or '약국' (pharmacy). In speech, staff often just say '안으로 들어가세요' (please go inside).

examples.en: The doctor examines the patient.
The doctor examined the child's throat.

examples.ko: 오늘은 오후 두 시부터 진찰할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Today we can see patients from two in the afternoon.
After examining me, the doctor prescribed medicine.

examples.ko: 진찰하는 동안 환자는 조용히 앉아 있었어요.
examples.en: The patient sat quietly during the examination.

examples.ko: 배가 아픈 이유를 알려면 직접 진찰해서 확인해야 해요.
examples.en: To know why your stomach hurts, the doctor has to examine you directly.

explain: 의사가 환자의 몸 상태를 살펴볼 때 쓰기 때문에 주어는 보통 의사예요. 환자가 병원에서 의사를 만나는 일은 '진료를 받다', '진찰을 받다'라고 해요. '제가 진찰했어요'는 의사가 아니면 어색해요.
explain_en: It is used when a doctor checks a patient, so the subject is normally the doctor. A patient seeing a doctor says '진료를 받다' or '진찰을 받다'. '제가 진찰했어요' sounds odd unless you are a doctor.

examples.en: How many floors does this building have?
The higher the floor, the better the view.

examples.ko: 집을 구할 때 층수도 꼭 확인해요.
examples.en: When I look for a home, I always check the floor number too.
If the floor is low, it can be noisy.

examples.ko: 엘리베이터 안의 층수 표시가 고장 났어요.
examples.en: The floor indicator inside the elevator is broken.

examples.ko: 저는 너무 높지 않은 층수를 좋아해요.
examples.en: I like a floor that is not too high.

explain: '몇 층이에요?'는 한 층을 묻고, '층수'는 건물이 몇 층인지나 집이 몇 층인지를 숫자로 이야기할 때 써요. '층수가 높다/낮다'처럼 말하고, 집을 구할 때 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '몇 층이에요?' asks about one floor, while '층수' is used when talking about floor numbers, either how tall a building is or which floor a home is on. You say '층수가 높다/낮다' (the floor is high/low), and it comes up a lot when looking for a home.

examples.en: On election day they check your ID at the polling place.

examples.ko: 이사하면 투표는 어디서 해요? — 새 주소지 근처 투표소로 가면 돼요.
examples.en: Where do I vote if I move? — Just go to the polling place near your new address.
The polling place is close to my home, so I walked.

examples.ko: 투표소 앞에 사람들이 길게 줄을 섰어요.
examples.en: People lined up in a long queue in front of the polling place.

examples.ko: 투표소는 아침 여섯 시에 문을 열어요.
examples.en: The polling place opens at six in the morning.

examples.ko: 투표소 안에서는 큰 소리로 이야기하지 마세요.
examples.en: Please don't talk loudly inside the polling place.

explain: 선거 날에 투표하는 장소예요. 학교나 주민센터가 투표소가 되는 경우가 많아요. 미리 투표하는 곳은 '사전투표소'라고 따로 불러요.
explain_en: It is the place where you vote on election day. Schools and community centers are often used as polling places. A place for early voting is called a '사전투표소' separately.

examples.en: I got my room key at the hotel front desk.

examples.ko: 프런트에 가서 수건을 더 달라고 했어요.
examples.en: I went to the front desk and asked for more towels.
The front desk staff were very kind.

examples.ko: 프런트가 오후 두 시부터 체크인을 받아요.
examples.en: The front desk accepts check-in from two in the afternoon.
The front desk is in the lobby on the first floor.

examples.ko: 프런트로 전화해서 택시를 불러 달라고 했어요.
examples.en: I called the front desk and asked them to call a taxi.

explain: 주로 호텔이나 회사 입구에서 손님을 맞는 곳을 말해요. '프론트'라고 쓰는 경우도 있지만 표준 표기는 '프런트'예요.
explain_en: It mostly means the place at the entrance of a hotel or company where guests are received. The spelling 프론트 is also seen, but the standard spelling is 프런트.
